subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli turn-end cleanup remain unconditional, or should OpenClaw add a bounded drain/telemetry contract for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren such as Workflow runtimes?
rationale: The source confirms the cleanup path, but changing it affects process-tree orphan prevention, user-visible task completion, config/default surface, and the boundary with Claude Code's own tool lifecycle.

options.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
options.body: Add a narrow contract that detects in-flight CLI-owned background children, defers cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfaces forced cleanup as parent-visible failure/telemetry.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep cleanup unconditional for now, but snapshot/log/surface killed grandchildren so the silent failure class is observable before changing process lifetime.

options.title: Declare unsupported post-turn work
options.body: Document or enforce that Claude CLI Workflow/background grandchildren cannot survive OpenClaw turn cleanup and route users to ACP, exec/process, or detached task surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded drain plus telemetry
recommendation.body: Add a narrow contract that detects in-flight CLI-owned background children, defers cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfaces forced cleanup as parent-visible failure/telemetry.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus introduced the warm Claude CLI live-session path and is closest to the lifecycle contract being decided.
